summary: This note, despite its title "Tanzania", actually covers the 2007-2010 financial crisis in the United States. It discusses comparisons to the Great Depression, the shadow banking system, the collapse of Countrywide and IndyMac, the money market and credit market freezes of 2008, and the causes debated among regulators and scholars, including subprime mortgages, government housing policy, and tail risk. It also outlines the regulatory proposals introduced by the Obama administration, including the Volcker Rule.
one_line: Overview of the 2007-2010 U.S. financial crisis, its causes such as shadow banking and subprime mortgages, and the regulatory response.
key_facts: Market strategist Phil Dow said the Dow Jones average's fall of more than 50% over 17 months was similar to a 54.7% fall in the Great Depression.
Floyd Norris of The New York Times wrote in March 2009 that the decline had not been a mirror image of the Great Depression because rates of decline started much faster in 2007.
In a June 2008 speech, Timothy Geithner blamed a "run" on entities in the "parallel" banking system, also called the shadow banking system, for freezing credit markets.
The U.S. recession that began in December 2007 ended in June 2009, according to the National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER).
Withdrawals from money markets were $144.5 billion during one week in September 2008, versus $7.1 billion the week prior.
The TED spread reached a record 4.65% on October 10, 2008.
NPR correspondents described a "Giant Pool of Money" represented by $70 trillion in worldwide fixed income investments seeking higher yields than U.S. Treasury bonds.
By September 2008, average U.S. housing prices had declined by over 20% from their mid-2006 peak.
During 2007, lenders began foreclosure proceedings on nearly 1.3 million properties, a 79% increase over 2006; in 2008 this rose to 2.3 million, an 81% increase.
By September 2009, 14.4% of all U.S. mortgages outstanding were delinquent or in foreclosure, up from 9.2% in August 2008.
The Senate passed a reform bill in May 2010, following a House bill passed in December 2009.
In January 2010, Obama proposed additional regulations limiting banks' proprietary trading, dubbed the "Volcker Rule" after Paul Volcker.
Raghuram Rajan delivered a paper in 2005, "Has Financial Development Made the World Riskier?", arguing that disaster might loom.
IndyMac reported that Moody's and Standard & Poor's downgraded MBS bonds in April 2008, including $160 million of bonds issued by IndyMac and retained in its portfolio.
The Office of Thrift Supervision seized Countrywide after its financial condition deteriorated, following lawsuits by California Attorney General Jerry Brown.

entities.name: Phil Dow
entities.role: market strategist who compared the current market malaise to the Great Depression

entities.name: Floyd Norris
entities.role: chief financial correspondent of The New York Times who wrote a March 2009 blog entry on the decline

entities.name: Timothy Geithner
entities.role: President and CEO of the New York Federal Reserve Bank who blamed runs on the shadow banking system; became Secretary of the United States Treasury in 2009

entities.name: Countrywide
entities.role: lender sued by California Attorney General Jerry Brown and seized by the Office of Thrift Supervision

entities.name: Jerry Brown
entities.role: California Attorney General who sued Countrywide for unfair business practices and false advertising

entities.name: Barack Obama
entities.role: United States President who introduced regulatory proposals in June 2009 and declared the markets stabilized in January 2010

entities.name: National Bureau of Economic Research
entities.role: U.S. body that dated the end of the recession to June 2009

entities.name: TIME magazine
entities.role: magazine that declared in April 2009 that the banking crisis was over

entities.name: Financial Crisis Inquiry Commission
entities.role: U.S. commission that dates the crisis to 2008 and whose majority and minority reports addressed housing policy

entities.name: Michael Greenberger
entities.role: former CFTC Division of Trading & Markets director who testified before the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation on June 3, 2008

entities.name: IntercontinentalExchange
entities.role: Atlanta-based exchange named by Greenberger as playing a key role in the speculative run-up of oil futures prices

entities.name: Paul Krugman
entities.role: economist who claimed the GSEs never purchased subprime loans, a claim widely disputed

entities.name: Paul Volcker
entities.role: publicly argued for the proposed changes that were dubbed the Volcker Rule

entities.name: Raghuram Rajan
entities.role: chief economist at the International Monetary Fund who predicted the crisis and delivered a critical paper in 2005

entities.name: Alan Greenspan
entities.role: chairman of the US Federal Reserve about to retire in 2005, honored at the event where Rajan delivered his paper

entities.name: IndyMac
entities.role: bank whose MBS bond ratings were downgraded in April 2008, affecting its risk-based capital ratio

entities.name: NPR
entities.role: broadcaster whose correspondents argued in a Peabody Award winning program that a Giant Pool of Money drove the crisis

entities.name: Moody's and Standard & Poor's
entities.role: credit rating agencies that downgraded many mortgage-backed security bonds in April 2008

entities.name: Office of Thrift Supervision
entities.role: regulator that decided to seize Countrywide

entities.name: Federal Reserve
entities.role: central bank that ran programs to purchase commercial paper and was given enhanced authority to wind down systemically important institutions under proposals
